plain.li: [en:line,theirs,!condolences] Enclosed: a sprig of {PLANT}, pressed flat in a book, which grows everywhere here and nowhere else I know of.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences] Enclosed: a leaf from the {TREE} by our gate, which turns this colour every year and which I wanted you to see.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences] Enclosed: a drawing of the {ANIMAL} that comes to our door every evening, by someone who has never been taught to draw. It is the one with the legs.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences] Enclosed: a drawing by one of the children here of what they think your people look like, from my description. The tall one is you. I did not say you were tall.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,!w:tribal] Enclosed: a map of the road between us, with the bad stretch marked, and the inn that waters its beer marked twice.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences] Enclosed: a ribbon from the fair, which I won for something, and cannot remember what.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences] Enclosed: a feather. I do not know what bird. It seemed too good to waste.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences] Enclosed: a few seeds from our garden. Plant them in the spring and see what comes up. We are not entirely sure ourselves.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences] Enclosed: a smooth stone from the river. It is just a stone. I liked it.
[en:line,theirs,condolences] Enclosed: a pressed flower from our hills, for the grave, if you will have it.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,w:tribal] With this, a cord of knotted grass: each knot is a good wish, and there are many knots.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,w:tribal] With this, a tooth from the {ANIMAL} the hunters brought home. It is lucky. It was not lucky for the {ANIMAL}.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,w:spacer] Enclosed: a data chip with a recording of our evening music. The quality is poor. The music is not.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,w:industrial] Enclosed: a photograph, a little blurred, of the whole town on the steps of the hall. I am the blur on the left.
[en:line,ours,!condolences,colony:children] Enclosed: a drawing by one of the children here, of what they think {TOWN} looks like. It has a great many towers.
[en:line,ours,!condolences,season:spring|season:summer] Enclosed: a flower from our fields, pressed flat. It will not smell of much by the time it reaches you, but it did once.
[en:line,ours,!condolences] Enclosed: a little map of the way to us, in case you are ever passing.
[en:line,ours,!condolences,season:autumn] Enclosed: a few seeds from our stores. Plant them in the spring.
[en:line,ours,!condolences,colony:harvest] Enclosed: a twist of this year's grain, so you can see what we grow.
[en:line,ours,!condolences,colony:animals] Enclosed: a tuft of fur from one of our animals, who sends regards.
[en:line,ours,condolences] Enclosed: a flower for the grave, if you will have it, from all of us.
[olde,en:line,theirs,!condolences] Herewith a sprig of {PLANT}, pressed in a book, that groweth all about us here.
[olde,en:line,theirs,!condolences] Herewith a ribbon from the fair, that I won for somewhat, and cannot remember what.
[olde,en:line,theirs,!condolences] Herewith a map of the road betwixt us, with the ill stretch marked, and the inn that watereth its ale marked twice.
[olde,en:line,theirs,!condolences] Herewith a leaf of the {TREE} by our gate, that turneth this hue each year.
[olde,en:line,theirs,condolences] Herewith a flower of our hills, for the grave, if thou wilt have it.
[olde,en:line,ours,!condolences] Herewith a little map of the way to us, should thou ever pass.
[olde,en:line,ours,condolences] Herewith a flower for the grave, from all of us.
[u:none,en:line,!condolences] i put in a fether
[u:none,en:line,!condolences] theres a rock in here. its a gud rock
[u:none,en:line,condolences] i put a flower in for the grave
[sv:fey,en:line,!condolences] Enclosed: a ring of mushrooms, pressed. Do not step in it. Do not step out of it either, once you have.
[sv:fey,en:line] Enclosed: one dewdrop, kept. It may have dried by the time you read this. That is its own kind of message.
[sv:beast,en:line,!condolences] With this, a scrap of cloth that smells of our den, so you will know us when we meet.
[sv:beast,en:line,!condolences] With this, a tooth, from the last hunt. It is lucky. We are sure of it.

[en:line,theirs,!condolences,their:scholars] Enclosed: an index card from the archive, cross-referencing you. You are filed under Correspondents, Pleasant, and also, by a clerical error, under Weather.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,their:traders] Enclosed: a price list, out of date, because it is always out of date by the time it reaches anyone. Use it to haggle.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,their:salvagers] Enclosed: a small gear from something we pulled out of the ground. We have no idea what it did. It seemed like the kind of thing you would like.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,their:crew] Enclosed: a hull rivet, polished. Everyone of the crew carries one. You are not crew, but you are close enough to carry a spare.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,their:seers] Enclosed: the tower's forecast for your country for the next month. It is probably wrong. It is beautifully drawn.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,their:linesmen] Enclosed: a length of the old wire, braided into a ring. The linesmen make them in the long nights on the masts.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,their:drillers] Enclosed: a little bottle of oil from the first gusher of the season. It is meant to be lucky. It is mostly sticky.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,their:vaultfolk] Enclosed: a picture of the sky. We take a great many of them. We are still not used to it.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,their:tamers] Enclosed: a ribbon from the ring, won by a beast who did not care for it at all.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,their:grovekeepers] Enclosed: a seed from the oldest tree in our grove. Plant it where it can grow for a hundred years, and then do not cut it.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,their:herders] Enclosed: a twist of wool from the first shearing, still smelling of sheep. You will not need to be told which sheep.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,their:editors] Enclosed: a seed, edited. It should come up {PLANT}, more or less. Report back.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,their:listeners] Enclosed: a slip of paper with the hum written on it, as near as it can be written. Read it aloud at night. Or do not.
[olde,en:line,theirs,!condolences,their:pilgrims] Herewith a pilgrim's badge from the shrine, of pewter, a little bent from the road.
[olde,en:line,theirs,!condolences,their:healers] Herewith a little bag of dried {PLANT}, for the stomach-ache, which the Order sendeth to all its friends.
[olde,en:line,theirs,!condolences,their:artisans] Herewith a shard of our best glaze, that thou mayst see the colour, and it beareth the mark.
[olde,en:line,theirs,!condolences,their:hunters] Herewith a feather from the lantern-post, where the owls sit and keep watch with us.
[olde,en:line,theirs,!condolences,their:sextons] Herewith a pressed flower from the bell-yard, where the quiet ones sleep. They will not mind.
[olde,en:line,theirs,!condolences,their:fishers] Herewith a fish-hook of bone, of the old making, for luck upon the water.
[olde,en:line,theirs,!condolences,their:mercenaries] Herewith a copper token of the Banner, such as is given to friends of the company. Show it at our camp, and thou shalt be fed.
[olde,en:line,theirs,!condolences] Herewith a sketch of our hall, done by one that thinketh themself a limner. The door is wrong. The rest is near enough.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,w:tribal,fam:familiar|fam:close] With this, a string of beads from the river, one for each moon since your words first came.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,w:tribal] With this, something the {ANIMAL} left behind on the trail, found, not taken. We do not take them.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,w:tribal] With this, a little bundle of sweet grass, braided. Burn a strand when the house feels heavy.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,w:spacer] Enclosed: a data chip with the night sky from our roof, recorded from dusk to dawn. It is mostly dark. The good part is near the end.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,w:industrial] Enclosed: a postcard of {TOWN} from the printer's, showing the main street on a sunny day, which it has had at least once.
[en:line,theirs,condolences] Enclosed: a candle from our shrine, lit once for your loss and put out, so that you can light it again yourselves.
[en:line,theirs,condolences,w:tribal] With this, a little ash from our fire, where we sang for your dead.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,fam:familiar|fam:close] Enclosed: a copy of one of your letters, which I copied out because I wore the first one through. You will not need it. I wanted you to know.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,fam:close] Enclosed: a key to the gate at {TOWN}. You know where we are. Come.
[en:line,ours,!condolences,fam:close] Enclosed: a little drawing of our gate, so that when you finally come you will know it from the others.
[en:line,ours,!condolences,season:autumn] Enclosed: a leaf from the first tree to turn here this year. We argued about which tree. This one won.
[en:line,ours,!condolences,season:winter] Enclosed: nothing, because the thing I meant to enclose was snow, and I have learned that it does not travel.
[en:line,ours,!condolences,colony:harvest] Enclosed: a twist of seed from our harvest, the best of it, for your own fields if you want it.
[sv:green,en:line,!condolences] Enclosed: a seed. It is one of our cousins. Please plant it somewhere with afternoon light. It will write to you in its own way.
[sv:green,en:line,!condolences] Enclosed: a leaf. It was ours. Now it is yours. That is what leaves are for.
[sv:machine,en:line,!condolences] ATTACHMENT: ONE (1) PRESSED FLOWER. THIS UNIT WAS INFORMED THAT HUMANS ENJOY THESE. THIS UNIT HAS PRESSED IT VERY FLAT.
[sv:machine,en:line,!condolences] ATTACHMENT: ONE (1) DRAWING OF THIS UNIT, BY A CHILD. ACCURACY: LOW. THIS UNIT HAS KEPT THE ORIGINAL AND SENDS A COPY.
[sv:ancient,en:line,!condolences] Enclosed: a coin from a kingdom that no longer exists. I was at its founding and at its end. The coin outlasted both, as coins do.
[sv:ancient,en:line,!condolences] Enclosed: a letter I wrote two hundred years ago to someone who died before it arrived. I thought it deserved a reader at last.
[sv:hive,en:line,!condolences] With this, one cell of our comb, empty, cleaned. Hold it to your ear. That is what home sounds like.
[sv:hive,en:line,!condolences] With this, a wax token. Every one of us touched it. It is warm from all of us.
[sv:beast,en:line,!condolences] With this, a pine cone the young ones played with all evening. They want you to have it. It is slightly chewed.
[sv:fey,en:line,!condolences] Enclosed: three hairs from a unicorn, or a horse; the light was poor. Keep them anyway. Keep them under your pillow, and dream sideways.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences] Enclosed: half a recipe card, the other half having been eaten. You may guess the rest.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences] Enclosed: a lucky stone with a hole in it, which you look through to see things as they really are. I have looked. Things are much the same.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,!w:tribal] Enclosed: a button, which came off my coat while I was writing this, and which I am sending on rather than sewing back, out of laziness and affection.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences] Enclosed: a feather the children found and insisted be sent to you in particular. They would not say why.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,season:spring] Enclosed: the first flower of the spring here, which by rights should be on someone's table, and is instead on its way to yours.
[en:line,theirs,!condolences,season:winter,!w:tribal] Enclosed: a paper snowflake, cut by the youngest here. It is a very square snowflake.
[en:line,ours,!condolences] Enclosed: a sketch of the view from our gate, so you can picture where these letters come from. The hill is smaller in life.
[en:line,ours,!condolences,colony:children] Enclosed: a drawing by one of our children of what they think {TOWN} looks like. You have, apparently, a castle and a dragon.
